name: Vantablack-CNX
description: Vantablack-CNX is a vertically-aligned carbon nanotube array coating material produced by Apex Nanofabrication, grown directly onto substrate surfaces via a catalytic CVD process to create a forest of aligned tubes that traps 99.97% of incident light across visible, near-infrared, and radar wavelengths through multiple internal reflections between tube walls. Unlike its historical predecessors, the CNX formulation has been ruggedized — the tube array survives handling, thermal cycling, and moderate abrasion through a sparse polymer infill that stabilizes the array without significantly reducing absorption. It is simultaneously the most visually striking and the most militarily sensitive material in routine commercial production.
cost: Φ 22,000 per square meter (civilian research grade); military pricing classified
story_hooks: Vantablack-CNX is tightly export-controlled and theoretically unavailable to civilian operators — yet someone has coated an entire vehicle with it and is operating in the Shelf district, invisible to every optical and radar sensor the city has.

A researcher at Apex Nanofabrication has found a way to deposit Vantablack-CNX on flexible substrates — creating a wearable coating that makes the wearer effectively invisible to surveillance systems. The research has disappeared along with the researcher.

A shipment of Vantablack-CNX panels listed as 'optical calibration equipment' has been cleared through civilian customs — someone with serious connections is moving military-grade stealth materials into private hands.
